soundness_flags.label: def:efficient-score-handle and thm:efficient-eif-bound
soundness_flags.one_line: The handle never specifies the conditional moment operator, projection coefficient, or resulting score equation, so the claimed canonical gradient and the estimator defined by its held-out equation are not yet mathematically determinate objects.

soundness_flags.label: def:regularized-inverse and thm:crossfit-attainment
soundness_flags.one_line: An L2(P) error bound alone does not define a global inverse-norm event for the learned covariance function, and no PSD projection or held-out-X quantifier is supplied to make the asserted 2/underline-kappa inverse bound well-defined.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:crossfit-attainment / honest_scope
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The result is conditional on fixed aggregate support, fixed T and joint residual dimension, and excludes singular covariance, unbalanced panels, repeated cross-sections, and adaptive aggregation weights.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Uniform attainment and Wald coverage are claimed only over the fixed-dimensional triangular subclasses M_n under the displayed nuisance-learning conditions.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper combines clean-comparison staggered-DDD estimates using weights summing to one and selects the minimum-variance constant GMM weight Omega^{-1}1/(1' Omega^{-1}1).
Theorem 5 gives the nonparametric efficient influence function for the canonical panel triple-difference parameter and the paper then constructs a cross-fitted estimator from it.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 16–17, equations (3.11)–(3.13) and Theorem 3.2; p. 20, equation (4.3)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper stacks staggered-DiD influence functions, uses their conditional covariance for inverse-covariance weighting, includes event-study target-share terms, and proposes plug-in covariance-weighted estimation.

The article derives semiparametric efficiency bounds for finite-dimensional parameters in sequential moment-restriction models with unknown functions and presents an optimally weighted orthogonalized estimator.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 2.1 and Section 3.1, Theorems 3.1–3.2 and Corollary 3.1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines Neyman-orthogonal scores and gives cross-fitted approximate-linearity, variance-estimation, and uniform-confidence results under high-level score and nuisance conditions.

The paper develops stacked DDD, describes its regression-transparency/efficiency tradeoff, and notes that shared control units generally make its within-stack just-identified GMM construction inefficient.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the efficient-score handle with an explicit stacked conditional-moment operator, target-share derivative, projection coefficient, and score equation; then define the cross-fitted statistic by that displayed score.

Define the covariance learner as a symmetric PSD projection followed by ridge regularization, state whether the inverse bound is pointwise at a held-out draw or uniform in x, and align the required norm/rate condition with that choice.

Add a DDD-specific corollary comparing the efficient aggregate to both Ortiz-Villavicencio–Sant'Anna constant GMM and Hsieh stacked DDD on a generic shared-comparison class, not only the two-comparator witness.

recommended_next_step: Revise the score and inverse constructions into explicit well-defined objects, then rerun the field-tier novelty review.
